subject: Streaming SLO qual: concurrency & latency calibration + harness artifacts
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@cartwheel.com>, Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@cartwheel.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Recap + concrete asks: streaming SLOs, concurrency targets, harness artifacts

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to walk through Cartwheel's streaming use case in detail. Quick recap and our asks so we can get the qualification run scheduled: 

Key notes from today:
- Primary workflow: real-time promo personalization stream; average prompt length ~120 tokens, but peak prefix hits include long context up to 1,200 tokens (cart + session history).
- Target P99 latency for streaming first-token: 120 ms (p95 target 60 ms) for the baseline 8k token model.
- Expected concurrency: sustained 300 concurrent streams during peak, short spikes up to 1,200 concurrent sessions for flash sales.
- Throughput requirement (tokens/s): ~18k tokens/s sustained across the pool.

Concrete asks we need from Cartwheel to reproduce and qualify:
1) Prompt set: canonical prompt samples + distribution (short, medium, long). CSV or JSONL with sample metadata (approximate token counts).
2) Typical session pattern: how often do you send prefix updates vs. single-turn messages? Provide a small trace or a RPS curve for a 10-minute peak slice.
3) Success criteria: confirm that P99-first-token ≤ 120 ms and error rate ≤ 0.5% at 300 sustained concurrency.
4) Any throughput ceilings per-customer (e.g., rate limits or burst throttles) we should emulate?

What we'll deliver once we have artifacts:
- A reproducible harness run (we'll share the harness_instructions.md and a sample invocation) with the prompt_pack_v2.csv you provide.
- Measurement definitions: exact metric names (p95/p99 first-token, per-stream token/sec, kv-cache hit ratio) and how we compute them.
- Baseline run on our hosted infra and an optional run on a dedicated pool if you want capacity parity.

Next steps / timeline:
- If you can drop the prompt pack + a short 10-minute sequence trace by EOD Monday, we can schedule an initial run on Wed and get back a readout by Friday.

Thanks — I'll queue the harness and allocate an SE (Marissa) to validate the traces.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — adding two quick clarifications from the commercial/ops side so Alex and Ben know what we'll need for an apples-to-apples qualification: 

- Pricing/commitment note: if Cartwheel wants the qualification run on dedicated capacity we need to lock in a 3-month reserved window for the sustained concurrency run; otherwise we can run it on hosted capacity for a one-off readout.
- Data handling: please indicate whether any prefix data is PII or needs to be redacted before you share sample traces. We can accept redacted examples and note the impact on generation behavior in the readout.

Alex — two quick asks to unblock us:
1) Can you confirm whether you prefer a hosted one-off versus dedicated precommitted capacity for the test?
2) If anything in your sample prompt pack is sensitive, please redacted fields as <REDACTED> and include token counts so we can preserve distribution.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Cc: Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@cartwheel.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap + concrete asks: streaming SLOs, concurrency targets, harness artifacts

Appreciate the clear recap. Attaching the initial artifacts — cleaned for PII and annotated with token counts. A few notes inline:

Attachments included:
- prompt_pack_v2.csv — 1200 rows, columns: sample_id, intent_group, approx_tokens, template_variation.
- sample_payloads.jsonl — 10k lines that simulate 10 minutes of peak; includes session_id, event_type (prefix/update/complete), and approx_tokens.

Notes/constraints:
- We can only share redacted session ids; real user ids have been replaced with stable pseudonyms.
- For dedicated capacity: we can do a 3-month pilot but need pricing scoping from your side — Kimberly, can you drop an initial ballpark?
- During flash sale spikes, the concurrency distribution skews heavily — ~55% of streams are short (<5s), but these still cause connection density on the routing tier. We included a CSV column "spike_flag" to mark sampled flash-sale events.

We'll upload the CSV and JSONL to the Drive link you shared and set permissions for redwood-internal. Expect the upload by EOD Monday.

— Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Product Engineering, Cartwheel

Subject: Re: Recap + concrete asks: streaming SLOs, concurrency targets, harness artifacts

Perfect — thanks Alex (and Ben). Once we have the uploaded artifacts I'll run the harness with three passes: 

1) Calibration (hosted, single-pool) — confirm metric definitions and verify harness playback fidelity against your sample_payloads.jsonl.
2) Sustained run (hosted or dedicated per your preference) — target 300 sustained concurrency for 10 minutes; measure p95/p99 first-token, per-stream token/sec, and error rates.
3) Spike run — run the flash-sale spike using the sample set's spike_flag to reproduce the 1,200 concurrent short streams pattern and observe tail latency/backpressure behavior.

Deliverables by Friday after we run: readout deck, raw logs (aggregated metrics + per-stream traces), and an operations checklist that maps observed bottlenecks to recommended levers (batch size, kv-cache TTLs, routing policy tweaks).

If Cartwheel will consider dedicated capacity, Kimberly — happy to schedule a scoping call after you send the ballpark pricing. Alex — ping me here once assets are uploaded and I'll confirm the run window.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
